brandNote: a field log that works in the mud
h1: Every bird you saw, in the place you saw it, with no signal.
lede: Ternmark writes your sighting into a local database the moment you name it, and syncs when you get home. The estuary, the marsh and the eleven hours in between are all inside the app.

features.b: The species list, your map and your last four seasons are on the phone. Nothing asks for a network. Records queue, then merge, and a conflict is a row you can read.
Press and hold: six seconds of the marsh becomes a shortlist of nine species with the part of the call that matched, in a box you can reject.
One folder of CSV and GeoJSON on your machine, plus a plain-text export of every note. The app is a window onto it, not the only door.

stats.n: between the car park and the hide
on the device, in six seconds
name, count, note, and it is written

quote.q: I filled in the whole tide in the blackest part of the season, on a phone with no signal, in gloves. It was all there when I got back to the car, and it was all mine.
quote.role: county recorder, the Sandbar estuary, 11 seasons

foot.made: Ternmark is made by two people in a room above a boatyard at Upcerne.
foot.legal: Ternmark 2025. No trackers, no analytics, one cookie for your own settings.
foot.inputHint: About ten times a year, on the day they are published.
